name: Standing Barbell Strict Press
grip: Overhand, at or just outside shoulder width, with the bar supported securely in the hands.
description: Press a barbell from the upper chest to overhead while standing with the legs still.
setup: Set the rack just below shoulder height and take an overhand grip.
Unrack the bar to the upper chest, step clear and establish a balanced stance.
Brace the trunk with elbows slightly in front of the bar.
instructions: Move the head just enough to let the bar pass, then press upward without knee drive.
Allow the shoulder blades to rotate upward as the bar rises.
Finish with the bar balanced over the shoulders and midfoot, head neutral.
Lower under control to the upper chest, keeping the torso stable.
cues: Keep the ribs over the pelvis.
commonMistakes: Driving with the knees or leaning far backward.
Pressing behind the neck or letting the bar drift forward.

logging.example: A 20 kg bar plus two 15 kg plates: record 50 kg total.

variantNote: Standing front-of-neck strict barbell press. The generic alias Strict Press is mapped to this barbell variant; seated, dumbbell and push presses are distinct.
